How to Write Effective Test Cases A test case is a detailed set of steps used to validate one objective. Well-written test cases are simple, repeatable, and easy for another tester to execute without confusion. Include the following fields in every test case: Test Case ID – unique identifier Description or Scenario – what is being validated Preconditions – setup needed before execution Steps – execution actions Expected Result – expected system behavior Actual Result – observed outcome during execution Best practices for writing test cases: Keep one validation objective per test case Map each test case to a requirement or user story Include both positive and negative coverage Use clear and measurable expected results Write steps in the same order a user would perform them A good test case proves one thing clearly.
